subject: RFI: network segmentation, isolation model, and threat model
messages:
From: Carl Dunne <carl.dunne@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Sat, 01 Jun 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: network segmentation, isolation model, and threat model

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of Brightline's vendor security review for our enterprise rollout we need the following materials so our InfoSec team can complete their assessment:

- High-level network diagram showing control plane vs data plane, public endpoints, and per-tenant isolation boundaries.
- Short description of your isolation model (multi-tenant isolation, dedicated pools, and any hardware/software separation).
- Threat model summary (top threats, mitigations, assumed trust boundaries).
- Confirmation on key controls: KV cache encryption at rest/in transit, egress filtering, VPC peering options, KMS/HSM usage, and operational logging retention for 12 months.
- An editable spreadsheet version of your RFI answers where we can mark follow-ups.

Do you have these artifacts today? If so, could you share them and an estimated delivery for anything outstanding? We're aiming to close the security review by 2024-06-14.

Carl Dunne
Senior Security Engineer
Brightline Health
security@brightlinehealth.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: network segmentation, isolation model, and threat model

Carl —

Appreciate the clear asks. We have the majority of these artifacts and can deliver a consolidated package. Attached are: a first-pass network diagram (network-diagram-v3.png) and a one-page threat model summary (threat-model-summary.pdf). I'm also attaching an editable RFI spreadsheet (rfi_answers_v1.xlsx) with our initial responses — please flag rows you want us to expand.

Quick note on the isolation model: Redwood supports three serving modes — Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (customer-isolated GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Hosted customers, we enforce logical tenant isolation at the service and model layers, KV cache scoping per-tenant, and namespace separation in metadata stores. Dedicated and Private provide stronger isolation (hardware or VPC-level) per the contract.

We secure KV caches with TLS in transit; at-rest encryption is provided by the underlying storage layer and can be backed by customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. Egress policies and NAT controls are configurable for Dedicated and Private; Hosted customers use managed egress with filtering and monitoring.

I'll bring Rishi (networking) and Grace (product/security) into follow-ups for the technical deep-dive. If you want a walkthrough next week, we can schedule a 30–45 minute session.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Carl Dunne <carl.dunne@brightlinehealth.com>

Date: Sun, 02 Jun 2024 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: network segmentation, isolation model, and threat model

Thanks Hannah — got the initial package, helpful start. A few follow-ups from the InfoSec review:

1) KV cache encryption: can you confirm whether hosted KV caches are encrypted at rest by default, and whether BYOK (bring your own key) is offered for hosted customers? Brightline requires customer-managed keys for production PII workloads.
2) Egress & egress filtering: can Redwood supply a list of IP ranges and DNS policies used by hosted control and data planes? We need to allowlist them for our firewall testing.
3) Tenant isolation: the diagram is clear on logical boundaries; can you provide a short description of the threat mitigations for cross-tenant inference leakage (e.g., request scoping, model weights immutability, cache poisoning prevention)?
4) Logging & retention: confirm whether request traces and token-level logs are retained for 12 months in Dedicated and Private deployments, and what is available for Hosted customers (default retention and options to extend).

I've also attached a redlined copy of your RFI spreadsheet (RFI_Q_A_redline.xlsx) with inline questions (see sheet 'Security Followups').

Carl

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Jun 2024 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI redlines from Brightline — quick sync

Hannah/Grace — forwarding Carl's redlines. Quick notes from my side:

- KV cache encryption: For Hosted we currently encrypt at rest using provider-managed keys by default. BYOK is available for Dedicated customers and is on the roadmap for Hosted (expected H2 2024; we can provide interim contractual controls).
- Egress list: I'll generate a minimal allowlist (control-plane endpoints + managed egress ranges) — will need coordination with infra to timestamp planned IP changes.
- Cache poisoning / cross-tenant leakage: we enforce per-request tenant headers, use request-level namespace keys for the KV cache, and maintain immutable model artifacts per-deployment. We also run automated fuzz tests and periodic canary prompts to detect leakage.
- Logging retention: Hosted default is 90 days token-level logs; Dedicated can be configured to 12 months (contract-dependent). Private installs depend on customer storage retention policy.

Soojin — can you produce a focused network diagram callout that highlights egress points for the control plane vs data plane so we can deliver an annotated PNG?

Grace — can you prepare a 2–3 paragraph threat-model summary that calls out top threats (data exfiltration, model inversion, cache poisoning, compromised credentials) and our mitigations (isolation, encryption, runtime prompts, monitoring)?

I'll assemble answers for Carl and update the RFI spreadsheet.

—Rishi

Subject: Final: Brightline RFI — segmentation, isolation, and threat model (attachments included)

Carl —

Thanks again for the redlines. Please find our consolidated package attached and summarized below. We also updated the editable RFI workbook per your comments (sheet 'Security Followups' contains detailed answers). If you'd like, we can walk through these items in a 30-minute call this week.

Attachments included: network-diagram-v3.png (annotated), threat-model-summary.pdf (expanded), rfi_answers_v1.xlsx (updated with responses).

Executive summary (short):
- Isolation model: Redwood operates three serving modes. Hosted is logical multi-tenant with strict namespace separation and request-scoped caches; Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and customer VPC integration; Private delivers full VPC/on-prem separation with customer-managed KMS.
- KV cache encryption: Hosted uses provider-managed at-rest encryption today; Dedicated and Private support BYOK/KMS-backed encryption. We can include contract language for Brightline to require customer-managed keys on Dedicated.
- Egress/Allowlist: See the attached annotated diagram and Drive link for IP ranges. We will provide a formal allowlist CSV and coordinate a maintenance window for any planned changes.
- Threat model highlights: Top threats — cross-tenant data leakage, model inversion, cache poisoning, and credential compromise. Mitigations — per-tenant namespace keys, model artifact immutability, runtime request-scoping, rate-limiting, anomaly detection on outputs, and automated canaries for leakage detection. See threat-model-summary.pdf for details.
- Logging & retention: Hosted default token-level logging/trace retention is 90 days; Dedicated supports 12 months (configurable); Private is customer-managed. Audit logs for control-plane actions are retained 12 months for Dedicated and Private (SLA/contract dependent).

Next steps:
1) We'll upload a formal allowlist CSV and a short operational runbook to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE
2) If Brightline requires BYOK for Hosted during prod rollout, we'll scope contractual options and estimated delivery (target: Q3 2024 for hosted BYOK pilot).
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough — propose Wed 2024-06-05 10:00 AM PT or Thu 2024-06-06 2:00 PM PT. Please confirm.

Thanks — looping Rishi (network), Grace (threat model), and Soojin (network diagram) for any last clarifications.

Best,
